captures.note: Direct download, NOT a YouTube re-encode, so the sha256 will be a real identity rather than a record of what yt-dlp happened to pick that day. 640x480 H.264 + FLAC. Two properties make it unusually good ground truth for this production. (1) FLAC is lossless: alignment here is by audio cross-correlation, and the softsynth's output can be regenerated byte-exactly by work/re/runsynth.py, so the correlation is between two clean signals rather than against a lossy re-encode of a guess. (2) 640x480 matches the __640/__480 constants sitting in the binary's float pool, which suggests a native-resolution capture rather than a rescale. Fetch and pin locally: this host is not reachable from a cloud session (403 at the egress proxy), see docs/CLOUD_ENVIRONMENT.md. Capture is recorded, never distributed - work/reference/ is gitignored. MEASURED, 2026-08-17: alignmentOffsetMs=120 by work/re/capalign.mjs, agreed to the millisecond by all 27 of part one's windows at r 0.53-0.96 and 0 ppm drift. But the frame rate is 19001/634 = 29.97, and the intro runs at 50 Hz, so this has ALREADY been frame-rate converted and can never be a frame-exact oracle - it is a per-scene reference, not a per-frame one. Two further findings are in work/re/NOTES.md: the intro is silent for 1,852 ms between the parts, and our part three runs 2,640 ppm fast against this capture's clock.

FALLBACK, deliberately not captures[0]: tools/inspect/sweep.mjs reads captures[0], so this array's ORDER is load-bearing and the direct natami.pl file stays primary. A YouTube copy is re-encoded, which costs exactly the property that makes the primary source good here - lossy audio degrades the cross-correlation this production can otherwise run between two clean signals, since runsynth.py regenerates the soundtrack byte-exactly. Use this only if the direct file becomes unreachable. If both are ever fetched, check they are the same recording before trusting an offset measured against one for the other: duration, framing and frame rate all need comparing, and wonder's note in this repo is a standing reminder that frame RATE was the deficiency that mattered. CHECKED, 2026-08-17: both are fetched and they ARE the same recording - 446.346 s against 446.348 s. But nothing else about them matches. This one is 960x720 at 60 fps with Opus audio; the primary is 640x480 at 29.97 with FLAC. So this is the primary upscaled, frame-rate-doubled and re-encoded lossily, which is two conversions further from the Amiga and confirms it as the fallback. Its alignmentOffsetMs is deliberately still null: the primary's 120 ms was measured against the primary's own audio and must not be assumed to carry over.

status.note: web/ is SELF-CONTAINED: it downloads no recorded draw stream and no pre-rendered audio. engine.js decodes the scene graph and the geometry out of seg3 and seg4, runs _calc_matrix's three passes once per tick with the replayer's own effect-7 cues driving the beat sync, walks the nodes, clips and projects, and hands the result to the Warp3D shim; synth.js builds both DigiBooster modules byte-exactly from 99 KB of segments. All eight pipeline stages report a computed side. work/re/pipeline.mjs compares 140 frames against the recorded stream — 135 exact, 44,190 of 45,327 primitives matching on every vertex — and the five that differ are one geometry node whose displacement map is specified in PORT_SPEC and not yet reproduced. A 64k Mashi pack builds at 55,196 bytes against the original's 65,288: ./scripts/build-planet-potion-mashi.sh. The capture is fetched, pinned and aligned. See work/re/PORT_SPEC.md §0-bis for what is measured and what is left; docs/PLANET_POTION_FEASIBILITY.md is superseded by it.
